Answer all the questions.  
1A)           A loan of ₹20,000 requires monthly payments of ₹526 over a 48-month period of  
  time. These payments include both principal and interest.  
  i) What is the nominal interest rate for this loan?                                        (4)  
  ii) What is the effective interest rate per year?  
  iii) Determine the amount of unpaid loan principal after 24 months.  
  
1B)         The following data refers to the cash flows of five investment proposals. The total  
  money available to the company to invest is ₹35,000/-. The company can accept any one  
  of the proposals with the same letter or a combination of proposals with different letters  
  subject to the budget available. Select the best alternative based on the present worth of  
  the total investment criterion. The rate of return is 10%.

1C)         A working woman is planning for her retired life. She has 20 more years of service.          (3)

She earns ₹50,000 per month. She would like to deposit 10% of her salary at the end of  
  the first year and thereafter she wishes to increase the deposit amount every year by  
  ₹1,000 to the previous year for the next 14 years. At an interest rate of 15%, estimate  
  the total amount at the end of the 15th year.  
  
  
2A)    An industrial-grade asset was acquired for ₹5,00,000 to support critical production  
  operations. It has an expected useful life of 10 years, with a salvage value anticipated  
  to be ₹1,00,000 at the end of this period. Using the Declining Balance Depreciation  
  (4)  
  Method, calculate the undepreciated capital at the end of the 5th year. Also,  
  determine the depreciation charge for the 7th year.  
  
2B)    Two assets, X and Y, are being considered for selection based on their ability to  
  effectively perform a required operational function, each with unique financial  
  implications.  
  Asset Y requires an initial investment of Rs 34,000, with an anticipated salvage value  
  of Rs 4,500 at the end of a 4-year service life with operating expenses of Rs. 1,000  
  per year.  
  Asset X, on the other hand, has a lower initial cost, priced Rs 9,500 less than Y, yet  
  has a shorter economic lifespan by one year and no salvage value. Furthermore, X  
  incurs additional annual operating expenses of Rs 2,800 compared to Y. Given a  
  required rate of return of 15%, using study period of 3 years, determine which asset (3)  
  offers the more favourable financial outcome. Assume, the market value is equal to  
  book value and assets depreciate according to straight line method.  
  
  
2C)   Type 'A' bridge or Type 'B' bridge are under consideration which can be built as a part (3)

  annual maintenance costs will average \$400 per year and last forever. Type B bridge,  
  which must be replaced every 30 years, will cost \$40,000 to build and an annual  
  maintenance cost of \$700. Both bridges have no salvage value. Using capitalized cost  
  approach with an interest rate is 6%, which alternative is to be selected?

4C)      The manager of Erie Pvt. Ltd. is involved in a production planning process and  
  wishes to conduct a risk assessment using two scenarios, the worst case and best-case  
  scenarios, based on the company's current estimated levels. Based on the following  
  information about Erie Ltd, you must conduct a break-even analysis under these  
  scenarios. The manager adopts the pricing strategy that involves determining the  
  selling price of the product and then figuring out if it can be made at a cost lower  
  than that.  
  
  i) Under best case scenario the manager expects the selling price of ₹47,000, and the  
  variable cost of manufacturing the unit is ₹27,200. What could the company's fixed (3)  
  cost per year be to break even with sales of 18,000 units per year?  
  
  ii) Under the worst-case scenario, the manager expects the selling price dropping to  
  ₹36,000 and variable cost increasing to ₹30,000, in this situation what would be the  
  fixed cost per year to break even if the sales remain unchanged at 18,000 units per  
  year.  
  Based on the results of the break-even analysis for both the Best-Case and Worst-  
  Case scenarios, how do these help in the company's financial risk minimization and  
  decision-making?  
  
5A)      Why is the current ratio considered a key liquidity ratio in assessing a company's  
  financial health? How does it differ from the quick ratio, and why is the distinction   (2)  
  important?  
  
5B)   A frozen fish company is planning an expansion to a cold storage facility. Two alternative (4)  
  site design proposals are being considered at an interest rate of 10% after consideration of  
  risk in investments. Plant A requires an expenditure of \$350,000 for land, while Plant B  
  requires \$425,000. Assume that the land will be sold after 30 years at the same purchase  
  price. The buildings are expected to last 30 years, the compressors and related equipment  
  will last 10 years before requiring replacement. The annual maintenance of the any

compressor costs \$1,000 and increases by \$500 every year throughout the compressor's  
  life.  
  The energy costs of the facility are as given below and will increase throughout the  
  building's life. Neither the buildings nor the equipment is expected to have any salvage  
  value. With this information and the data provided below make an annual cost  
  comparison to determine which proposal is preferred.  
  
  
5C)             An equipment having a life of 15 years with an initial cost of \$12,100 is being  
  considered for replacement The salvage value of a one-year-old equipment is \$7,000  
  and this value then onwards decreases every year by an amount of \$300.The  
  maintenance and operating cost is \$1,200 in the first year and then onwards it is  
  expected to increase by \$1,000 every year in future years. Compute the economic life  
  $$of this asset and the minimum EUAC, with i=10\%.$$
